title: Autoimmune Bullous Disease — Initial Workup
subtitle: Stage-by-stage: clinical → biopsy → DIF → IIF → ELISA

items.label: Onset, duration, rate of blister formation
items.detail: Rapid onset (days) vs chronic (weeks–months). Fluctuating or progressive course. Document number and sites of new blisters per day.

items.label: Mucosal involvement — oral, ocular, nasal, anogenital
items.detail: CRITICAL: Always examine all mucosal surfaces. Oral erosions often precede skin blisters in pemphigus vulgaris by weeks to months. Ocular scarring in MMP requires urgent ophthalmology referral.

items.label: Blister character: tense vs flaccid; Nikolsky sign history
items.detail: Patients often report that blisters 'break easily' (flaccid — pemphigus) or 'stay intact' (tense — BP). Nikolsky sign: lateral pressure on normal skin causes new blister extension — positive in pemphigus.

items.label: Medication review — new drugs in past 3–12 months
items.detail: Drug-induced pemphigus: penicillamine, captopril, ACE inhibitors, thiol drugs. Drug-induced BP: DPP-4 inhibitors (gliptins), PD-1/PD-L1 checkpoint inhibitors, furosemide, amoxicillin. Drug-induced LABD: vancomycin. Discontinue suspected agent.

items.label: Age, sex, ethnicity — inform pre-test probability
items.detail: PV: 40–60 y, Ashkenazi Jewish and Mediterranean populations. BP: >70 y, associated neurological disease. DH: young adults, M>F, Northern European. PG: pregnancy (2nd–3rd trimester).

items.label: Paraneoplastic features: known malignancy, constitutional symptoms, refractory mucosal disease
items.detail: PNP strongly associated with NHL, CLL, Castleman disease, thymoma. Request CT chest/abdomen/pelvis if PNP is suspected. Mucosal erosions resistant to standard immunosuppression should raise suspicion.

items.label: Gastrointestinal symptoms (bloating, diarrhea, steatorrhea)
items.detail: GI symptoms suggest celiac disease in DH. Ask about gluten-free diet attempts. Family history of celiac or autoimmune thyroid disease.

items.label: Prior treatments and response
items.detail: Dapsone response within 72 h strongly supports DH. Rapid response to superpotent topical steroid supports BP. Lack of response to systemic steroids raises concern for PNP or EBA.

items.label: Skin survey: blister morphology, distribution, healing pattern
items.detail: Tense intact blisters on urticarial base → BP. Flaccid blisters with crusted erosions → pemphigus. Scarring + milia on extensors → EBA. Grouped vesicles on extensors/scalp/buttocks → DH.

items.label: Nikolsky sign — lateral pressure on perilesional skin
items.detail: Positive in active pemphigus. Apply gentle lateral pressure with finger on apparently normal perilesional skin — epidermal sheets slide off. Also perform Asboe-Hansen sign: direct pressure on blister roof extends blister laterally.

items.label: Complete mucosal exam: oral cavity, conjunctivae, nasal, anogenital
items.detail: Oral: inspect gingiva (desquamative gingivitis in MMP, erosions in PV), buccal mucosa, palate. Ocular: conjunctival injection, symblepharon, fornix shortening — urgent ophtho if any scarring. Anogenital: erosions, stenosis.

items.label: Document disease extent for activity scoring
items.detail: Use validated scoring tools: PDAI (Pemphigus Disease Area Index) for pemphigus — scores mucosal and skin domains separately. BPDAI (Bullous Pemphigoid Disease Area Index) for BP. Required for treatment response monitoring.

items.label: Age-appropriate skin cancer screen if anti-laminin 332 suspected (MMP)
items.detail: Anti-laminin 332 (epiligrin) MMP has ~25–30% association with internal malignancy (solid tumors). If DIF shows laminin 332 pattern, initiate cancer screening.

items.label: Site selection: intact early blister edge (perilesional, NOT center)
items.detail: Target the advancing edge of a fresh blister (ideally <24 h old). Blisters older than 48 h show secondary changes (inflammation, re-epithelialization) that obscure diagnostic features. Avoid completely ruptured or crusted erosions.

items.label: 4 mm punch biopsy into blister edge — submit in 10% buffered formalin
items.detail: Standard punch technique. Formalin fixation for routine H&E only. Do NOT use formalin for the DIF biopsy (separate specimen required). Orient the punch to include both blister and perilesional normal skin.

items.label: Key histologic findings to report
items.detail: Intraepidermal: Acantholysis (loss of cell-cell adhesion) — suprabasilar (PV), subcorneal/granular layer (PF), full-thickness (PNP). Subepidermal: Clean split at DEJ with eosinophils (BP), neutrophil microabscesses at papillary tips (DH), mixed (EBA inflammatory variant). Level of split guides DIF and serology interpretation.

items.label: SEPARATE biopsy from perilesional NORMAL-appearing skin within 1 cm of blister edge
items.detail: DIF requires fresh or Michel's medium-preserved tissue — NOT formalin. Take from normal-appearing skin immediately adjacent to (within 1 cm of) an active blister. Avoid sampling from within the blister itself or from old scarred areas.

items.label: Transport in saline, Michel's medium, or Zeus medium — NOT formalin
items.detail: Michel's (or Zeus) medium preserves immunoreactants for up to 3 weeks at room temperature. Normal saline is acceptable if processed within 12–24 h. Formalin destroys the immunoglobulins needed for DIF — the most common preventable diagnostic error.

items.label: DIF pattern interpretation
items.detail: Intercellular IgG + C3 (fishnet/honeycomb): Pemphigus vulgaris, PF. Linear IgG + C3 at BMZ: Bullous pemphigoid, MMP, EBA, PG. Linear IgA at BMZ: Linear IgA bullous dermatosis, MMP (IgA type). Granular IgA at dermal papillae tips: Dermatitis herpetiformis (pathognomonic).

items.label: Salt-split skin technique if linear BMZ pattern — distinguishes BP from EBA
items.detail: Patient skin or normal salt-split substrate: incubate in 1M NaCl for 72 h to split at lamina lucida. Apply patient serum (IIF) or re-probe DIF biopsy. Epidermal/roof pattern: BP, MMP (anti-BP180/BP230). Dermal/floor pattern: EBA (anti-Type VII collagen), some MMP (anti-laminin 332). Critical distinction for treatment selection.

items.label: IIF on monkey esophagus substrate — for pemphigus
items.detail: Patient serum applied to monkey esophagus or human skin substrate. Intercellular staining pattern confirms pemphigus. Sensitivity ~80% for PV. Titer correlates loosely with disease activity but ELISA is more quantitative.

items.label: IIF on salt-split human skin — for subepidermal ABDs
items.detail: Patient serum applied to 1M NaCl-split normal skin substrate. Differentiates BP (roof pattern) from EBA and anti-laminin 332 MMP (floor pattern). Can be performed even when DIF is negative or unavailable.

items.label: IIF titer — correlates with disease activity at population level
items.detail: IIF titer rises during flares and falls with remission for pemphigus. Less reliable in BP; ELISA BP180 levels are preferred for monitoring BP activity. Obtain baseline titer before initiating immunosuppression.

items.label: Anti-Dsg3 + anti-Dsg1 ELISA (pemphigus)
items.detail: Dsg3 alone: mucosal-dominant PV. Dsg3 + Dsg1: mucocutaneous PV. Dsg1 alone: pemphigus foliaceus. Sensitivity >95% for active PV by ELISA. Titer correlates with disease activity and predicts relapse — monitor every 3–6 months. PMID: 31448731.

items.label: Anti-BP180 NC16A + anti-BP230 ELISA (bullous pemphigoid)
items.detail: BP180 ELISA sensitivity ~90% for active BP; titer correlates with BPDAI score. BP230 sensitivity ~60%; adds value when BP180 negative. Both negative with clinical + DIF picture: consider EBA, MMP, or PG. PMID: 35538739.

items.label: Anti-Type VII collagen ELISA (EBA)
items.detail: Sensitivity ~50–70% (lower than for pemphigus/BP). A negative result does not exclude EBA. If salt-split dermal/floor pattern on IIF or DIF, send anti-Type VII collagen and refer to tertiary center if diagnosis unclear.

items.label: Anti-tissue transglutaminase (tTG) IgA + anti-endomysial IgA (DH / celiac)
items.detail: Anti-tTG IgA sensitivity ~98% for celiac; endomysial IgA specificity ~99%. Both used in DH workup. Anti-epidermal transglutaminase (eTG) IgA most specific for DH skin disease but not universally available. Also check total serum IgA to exclude IgA deficiency (false negatives). PMID: 35538739.

items.label: Anti-plakins panel if PNP suspected (periplakin, envoplakin, BPAG1/2)
items.detail: PNP ELISA: anti-envoplakin + periplakin IgG most sensitive (~75%). Anti-Dsg3 often also positive. If seronegative but clinical suspicion high, request immunoprecipitation or Western blot on epidermal proteins. Always perform malignancy workup in parallel. PMID: 31448731.

items.label: Small bowel biopsy (duodenal) — for DH celiac confirmation
items.detail: Villous atrophy on biopsy confirms celiac enteropathy. Required if GFD is planned as primary treatment. Perform while patient is on gluten-containing diet for diagnostic accuracy.

items.label: CT chest/abdomen/pelvis + PET-CT if PNP suspected
items.detail: Castleman disease (mediastinal/abdominal), CLL (lymphadenopathy/splenomegaly), thymoma (anterior mediastinal mass). Age-appropriate additional cancer screening if anti-laminin 332 MMP identified.

items.label: G6PD level before starting dapsone
items.detail: G6PD deficiency causes hemolytic anemia with dapsone — potentially life-threatening. Check before starting dapsone for DH or MMP. Also check CBC at 2 weeks after starting (dose-dependent methemoglobinemia occurs in all patients; monitor Hgb and methHgb).

items.label: Disease activity scoring at baseline: PDAI or BPDAI
items.detail: PDAI (Pemphigus Disease Area Index): scores skin (lesion number/size) + oral + other mucosal domains. Total >45 = severe. BPDAI for BP. Mandatory before initiating treatment; repeat at each visit to document response.

items.label: Pre-immunosuppression screening: hepatitis B/C, quantiferon/TB, varicella IgG
items.detail: Rituximab: HBsAg, anti-HBc, HCV Ab (reactivation risk). High-dose prednisone: TB screening, VZV serostatus. Vaccinate VZV-naïve patients before immunosuppression if time permits.
